title: Miang Kham (Leaf-Wrapped Bites with Palm Sugar Sauce)
summary: A platter of fresh leaves with diced lime, ginger, shallot, chilli, peanuts, toasted coconut and dried shrimp, plus a sticky palm sugar and shrimp sauce, for wrapping one-bite parcels.
equipment: pestle and mortar or mini chopper

ingredients.item: fresh ginger, peeled and cut into 5 mm dice
betel leaves (cha plu), or 8 cm squares of collard greens
lemongrass stalk, pale part only, thinly sliced
palm sugar, grated, or dark brown sugar

steps.title: Toast
steps.text: Stir the coconut in a dry wok over medium heat for 2-3 minutes, until evenly nut-brown. Tip onto a plate straight away, as it burns quickly, and keep 2 tbsp aside for the sauce.

steps.title: Soak
steps.text: Cover the 1 tbsp dried shrimp for the sauce with hot water and leave for 15 minutes, then drain.

steps.title: Aromatics
steps.text: Wipe the wok, add the lemongrass, sliced shallot and galangal and dry-roast over medium heat for 4-5 minutes, stirring, until fragrant and dry. Roasting deepens their flavour.

steps.title: Pound
steps.text: Pound or blitz the roasted aromatics with the soaked shrimp and shrimp paste to a fine paste.

steps.title: Sauce
steps.text: Put the paste, palm sugar, fish sauce and water in a small pan and bring to the boil, stirring, then bubble for 2-3 minutes, until syrupy. Cool completely, then stir in the reserved coconut; it thickens as it cools.

steps.title: Lime
steps.text: Cut the lime, peel and all, into 5 mm dice, removing any pips.

steps.title: Platter
steps.text: Arrange the leaves, lime, ginger, shallots, peanuts, chillies, dried shrimp and toasted coconut in small piles, with the sauce in a bowl. To eat, hold a leaf in your palm, add a little of each, top with a small spoon of sauce, fold and eat in one bite.

tips: Betel leaves are sold in Thai and Vietnamese shops; collard greens or Chinese broccoli leaves, cut into squares, work too.
If the sauce sets too thick once cold, loosen it with a teaspoon of warm water.
Keep the chillies on the side so everyone can choose the heat.
storage: The sauce keeps for 1 week in the fridge. Prepare the platter just before serving; the cut lime and shallot keep for a few hours, covered and chilled. Cool leftovers in a shallow container and refrigerate within 2 hours (within 1 hour on a day above 32°C).
